description: The objective of the Rodent Research-10 mission (RR-10) was to investigate how spaceflight affects the cellular and molecular mechanisms of normal bone tissue regeneration in space. To this end, ten (10) 14-15 weeks-old female B6129SF2/J Wild Type (WT), and ten (10) 14-15 weeks-old female B6;129S2-Cdkn1atm1Tyj/J (p21-null) mice received a pre-flight subcutaneous injection of the bone marker (Alizarin Red), and were then delivered to the ISS aboard SpaceX-21. At 7 days before euthanasia, all 20 mice received an intraperitoneal (IP) injection with a bone formation marker (Calcein). At 48 +/- 2 hours before euthanasia, all 20 mice received an IP injection with a second dose of Calcein as well as a cell proliferation marker (BrdU). Then, following 28-29 days in microgravity, the Flight mice were euthanized. Following removal of hindlimbs, carcasses were wrapped in aluminum foil, preserved in the CryoChiller, and stored at -80 C or colder until return to Earth. In addition to the Flight group, three ground control groups were also part of the study: Basal (representing the pre-launch state), Vivarium (standard vivarium housing for the same duration of time as flight), and Ground (flight habitat in the International Space Station Environment Simulator, ISSES). Twenty mice (10 of each strain) were included in each of these control groups (except Vivarium which included 12 of each strain). These were treated, euthanized and processed on the same schedule and in the same manner as the flight samples. This study includes bulk RNA sequencing ribodepleted gene expression data from 10 Basal animals (5 WT and 5 p21-null), 9 Flight animals (4 WT and 5 p21-null), 10 Ground animals (5 WT and 5 p21-null), and 10 Vivarium animals (5 WT and 5 p21-null).
funding: The sequencing analysis was funded by the NASA Space Biology program within the NASA Science Mission Directorate's (SMD) Biological and Physical Sciences (BPS) Division.

payloads.description:
Rodent Research-10 (RR-10) investigates the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying bone regenerative deficits due to disuse on Earth and microgravity in space. This mission examined how aging influences the regenerative potential of the femoral bone marrow stem cell populations.  Specifically, the study examined the role of a gene – Cdkn1a – that produces the CDKN1A protein – that inhibits cell cycle progression in cells. RR-10 (20 female mice, 13-17 weeks old, B6129SF2/J Wild Type (WT) and B6;129S2-Cdkn1atm1Tyj/J (p21-null) to assess the CDKN1a/p21 pathway in regenerative bone formation. The mice will be maintained on the ISS for ~30 days.  This mission was sponsored by NASA.

Tissue degeneration and the failure of tissue to regenerate normally in microgravity are increasing concerns for sustaining life in space, as the duration of future flight missions increase. The cellular mechanisms activated by microgravity unloading in mouse bone during spaceflight are not completely understood, but they include inhibition of the differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells and activation of the CDKN1a/p21-mediated cell cycle arrest in proliferative osteoprecursor cells on the bone surface.

In addition to the Flight group, three ground control groups were also part of the study: Basal (representing the pre-launch state), Vivarium (standard vivarium housing for the same duration of time as flight), and Ground (flight habitat in the International Space Station Environment Simulator, ISSES). Twenty mice (10 of each strain) were included in each of these control groups (except Vivarium which included 12 of each strain). These were treated, euthanized and processed on the same schedule and in the same manner as the flight samples. This study includes spatially resolved transcriptional profiling data from hippocampi from 5 WT flight animals, and 5 WT ground control animals. Hippocampi from the right hemisphere were embedded and cryosectioned. Cryosections were placed on gene expression arrays, stained and imaged. Imaging was followed by tissue permeabilization to release mRNA molecules from cells for capture onto the array surface. Subsequently, spatial transcriptomics libraries were prepared and sequenced.

PI: Eduardo Almeida, Ph.D.
Co-Investigators: Elizabeth Blaber, Ph.D., Ruth Globus, Ph.D., Yasaman Shirazi-Fard, Ph.D., Cassandra Juran, Ph.D.

The mission objectives

To test, in vivo, the hypothesis that CDKN1a/p21 is the key effector of cell cycle arrest in bone tissue in response to the stresses of spaceflight, the following specific aims of the Role of CDKN1a/p21 Pathway in Microgravity-Induced Bone Tissue Regenerative Arrest – A Spaceflight Study of Transgenic CDKN1a/p21-Null Mice in Microgravity (Rodent Research-10) investigation are addressed:

•	Determine and compare the extent of osteoblast proliferation, differentiation, and mineral deposition in microgravity and in 1g (Earth gravity equivalent) in a CDKN1a/p21-null mutant versus wild type (WT) mice.
•	Assess whether the coupling and balance of increased osteoclastogenesis and decreased osteoblastogenesis in microgravity is altered in a CDKN1a/p21-null background.
•	Determine whether CDKN1a/p21 expression in microgravity is regulated via mRNA stabilization by the microgravity-induced Cold Induced RNA Binding Protein (CIRBP) in response to oxidative stress in bone.

When completed, these studies will allow researchers to determine whether the presence of CDKN1a/p21 during mechanical unloading in microgravity induces arrest of bone growth and regeneration in vivo. The results from these studies also provide researchers with information to evaluate how CDKN1a/p21-mediated inhibition of osteoblast proliferation and differentiation may be coupled to osteoclastic activity induced by microgravity. Furthermore, these studies seek to connect the potential effector molecular mechanism of regenerative arrest in bone (by CDKN1a/p21) to its inducer, hypothesized here to be stabilization of CDKN1a/p21 message RNA by the oxidative (and other) stress response gene CIRBP.


IACUC Protocol Number:  RR-10

All animal procedures performed in these experiments were approved by the Institutional Animal Care and use Committees (IACUC) numbers NASA: RR-10 for flight at the NASA Ames Research Center (ARC) and the Kennedy Space Center (KSC) and the methods were carried out in accordance with relevant guidelines and regulations.

NASA Space Biology Biospecimen Sharing Program Activities 

The NASA Space Biology Biospecimen Sharing Program collected biospecimens from RR-10 to maximize the scientific return from the biological spaceflight.  The collected tissues included the following:  Duodenum., Jejunum, Pancreas, Stomach.


Available Data

The RR-10 payload produced the following Data (from checklist Excel file):

-	Animal enclosure temperature and relative humidity flight and ground data
-	Live Animal Return sensor accelerometer data 
-	ISS cabin and ground simulation chamber environmental monitoring data  
-	Rodent data including preflight data, operations time logs, sample shipment data.

projectTitle: The Role of P21/CDKN1a Pathway in Microgravity-Induced Bone Tissue Regenerative Arrest - A Spaceflight Study of Transgenic P21/CDKN1a Null Mice in Microgravity

protocols.description: Twenty (20) mice (female, 10 B6129SF2/J Wild Type (WT) and 10 B6;129S2-Cdkn1atm1Tyj/J (p21-null), 14-15 weeks old) were launched in one Transporter on SpaceX-21 (SpX-21) on December 6, 2020. The Flight (FL) mice were transferred into two Rodent Habitats upon arrival to the International Space Station (ISS) and were maintained in microgravity for 28-29 days. At 7 days before euthanasia (December 26 and 27, 2020), all 20 mice received an intraperitoneal (IP) injection with the bone formation marker (Calcein). At about 48±2 hours before euthanasia (December 31, 2020 and January 1, 2021), all 20 mice received an IP injection with a second dose of Calcein as well as the cell proliferation marker (BrdU). At approximately 28-29 in microgravity (January 2 and 3, 2021), the Flight mice were euthanized with a Ketamine/Xylazine cocktail, followed by cardiac puncture and thoractomy. Following skin removal, both hindlimb quarters were removed and preserved or fixed. Each carcass was wrapped in aluminum foil, preserved in the CryoChiller, and stored at -80C or colder until return to PI. Two other groups of mice, 20 for Ground Control (GC) and 24 for Vivarium Control (VC), half B6129SF/J Wild Type (WT) and half B6;129S2-Cdkn1atm1Tyj/J (p21-null), were selected by the PI and underwent the same procedures and treatment as the Flight group but with an offset of 3 days. In addition to the IP injections (Calcein and BrdU) described above, all mice in the FL, GC, and VC groups also received a pre-flight subcutaneous injection of the bone marker (Alizarin Red). Twenty (20) female mice (half WT and half p21-null) were selected by the PI for the Baseline Control (BL) group. Following a successful Launch, baseline animals were injected with Calcein at the time of Launch (7 days prior to dissection) and at 48±2 hours before dissection. BL animals were also injected with BrdU at 48±2 hours before dissection. Baseline dissections were performed 7 days after launch following the same procedures used for the Flight animals. The study followed recommendations in the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals and the protocol was approved by the NASA Flight Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
protocols.name: Animal Husbandry

protocols.description: At the end of RR-10 experiment, all frozen carcasses and preserved hindlimbs were returned to the PI. In May 2021, the Biospecimen Sharing Program (BSP) team performed complex, integrated dissections at NASA Ames Research Center with the Principal Investigator team. Colon tissues were preserved in RNAlater after dissection. Samples were kept at -80C freezer until processing. GeneLab only processed 9 FLT samples (4 WT and  5 p21-null), 10 GC samples (5 WT and 5 p21-null), 10 VIV samples (5 WT and 5 p21-null), and 10 BSL samples (5 WT and 5 p21-null) in this dataset.
protocols.name: sample collection

protocols.description: RNA was extracted using the AllPrep DNA/RNA Mini Kit (Qiagen, Valencia, CA) following GeneLab SOP 3.1-Qiagen AllPrep DNA/RNA Mini with Qiagen RNase-Free DNase set. Homogenization buffer for RNA purification was made by adding 1:100 beta-mercaptoethanol to Buffer RLT (Qiagen, Valencia, CA) and kept on ice until use. Approximately 20 mg of tissue was isolated using a scalpel, weighed and immediately placed in 600 uL of the Buffer RLT solution. Homogenization was performed using tissue homogenizing bead mix (Navy, Next Advance) on Bullet Blender Gold 24 (Next Advance) for 3 minutes at 4C and speed on 12 per SOP 2.1-Tissue homogenization Using Bullet Blender Gold Bead Beater. Homogenates were centrifuged for 5 minutes at 4C and 14,000 g to remove cell debris. Supernatant corresponding to 20mg of tissue from each sample was then used to isolate and purify DNA and RNA following the manufacturer protocol. RNA was eluted in 50 uL RNAse-free water and DNA was eluted in 50 uL RNAse-free water. Concentration for all RNA samples were measured using Qubit 3.0 Fluorometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA) with Qubit RNA BR kit following SOP 4.1-RNA/DNA/miRNA/cDNA Quantification using Qubit Fluorimeter. RNA quality was assessed using the Agilent 4200 TapeStation with the Agilent RNA ScreenTape (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA). GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.
protocols.name: Nucleic Acid Extraction

protocols.description: ERCC ExFold RNA Spike-In Mixes (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, Cat 4456739, v92), Mix 1 or Mix 2, were added on the day of library prep at the concentrations suggested by the manufacturer protocol. Protocol followed is SOP 5.2 Use of ERCC Spike-In Mixes and UMRR/UHRR Controls for Total RNA Sequencing. GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.
protocols.name: Spike-in Protocol

protocols.description: RNA ribo depletion and library preparation was done with Illumina TruSeq Stranded Total RNA Library Prep Gold (Illumina Inc., San Diego, CA). Input RNA were approximately 500 ng with RIN greater than 4. Index adapters used were at 1.5 uM (IDT, 384-well xGen Dual Index UMI Adapters). 15 cycles PCR were performed. Library fragment size was assessed using Agilent 4200 TapeStation with D1000 DNA ScreenTape (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA) following GeneLab SOP 6.3 Quality analysis of sequencing libraries using 4200 TapeStation System with D1000 reagent kit. Pooled library concentration was measured by Qubit 4 Fluorometer (ThermoFisher Scentific, Waltham, MA) following SOP 4.1-RNA/DNA/miRNA/cDNA Quantification using Qubit Fluorimeter. Library quality assessment was performed on iSeq100 (Illumina, San Diego, CA). GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.
protocols.name: Library Construction

protocols.description: RNA sequencing was performed by GeneLab Sample Processing Lab on Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Sequencing was set up as following: Read 1: 151bp, Index1: 17bp, Index2: 8bp Read 2:151bp. PhiX included as control and to increase library diversity. Protocol followed is SOP 7.1-Setting up NovaSeq 6000 and iSeq 100 Sequencers. GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.
protocols.name: Nucleic Acid Sequencing

protocols.description: Raw fastq files from each sample were assessed for % rRNA using HTStream SeqScreener (version 1.3.2) screened against a fasta file of Mus musculus rRNA sequences retrieved from NCBI on Sep-2021. Raw fastq file quality was evaluated with FastQC (version 0.12.1) and MultiQC (version 1.26) was used to generate MultiQC reports.
protocols.name: GeneLab raw data processing protocol

protocols.description: Data were processed as described in GL-DPPD-7101-G (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/blob/master/RNAseq/Pipeline_GL-DPPD-7101_Versions/GL-DPPD-7101-G.md), using NF_RCP version 2.1.0 (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/tree/NF_RCP-2.1.0/RNAseq/Workflow_Documentation/NF_RCP). In short, raw fastq files were filtered using Trim Galore! (version 0.6.10) powered by Cutadapt (version 4.2). Trimmed fastq file quality was evaluated with FastQC (version 0.12.1), and MultiQC (version 1.26) was used to generate MultiQC reports. Mus Musculus STAR and RSEM references were built using STAR (version 2.7.11b) and RSEM (version 1.3.3), respectively, Ensembl release 112, genome assembly GRCm39 (Mus_musculus.GRCm39.dna.primary_assembly.fa) concatenated with ERCC92.fa from ThermoFisher (https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/ERCC92.zip), and the following gtf annotation file: Mus_musculus.GRCm39.112.gtf concatenated with the ERCC92.gtf file from ThermoFisher (https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/ERCC92.zip). Trimmed reads were aligned to the Mus Musculus + ERCC STAR reference with STAR (version 2.7.11b) and alignment log files were compiled with MultiQC (version 1.26). Aligned reads were assessed for strandedness using RSeQC infer_experiment.py (version 5.0.4), gene body coverage using RSeQC geneBody_coverage.py (version 5.0.4), inner distance was assessed using RSeQC inner_distance.py (version 5.0.4), and distribution of RNA features using RSeQC read_distribution.py (version 5.0.4). Aligned reads from all samples were quantified using RSEM (version 1.3.3), with strandedness set to forward and RSEM count log files were compiled with MultiQC (version 1.26). To create a set of rRNA-removed quantification data, Ensembl IDs mapping to ribosomal RNA (rRNA) were removed from the RSEM gene count data. Both the original set of RSEM quantification data and the rRNA-removed data were subject to differential gene expression analysis as follows. A runsheet was generated with dp_tools (version 1.3.8) and the runsheet and quantification data were imported to R (version 4.4.2) with tximport (version 1.34.0), ERCC genes were removed, and the non-ERCC genes were normalized with DESeq2 (version 1.46.0) median of ratios method. Normalized gene counts were subject to differential expression analysis. Differential expression analysis was performed in R (version 4.4.2) using DESeq2 (version 1.46.0); all groups were compared pairwise using the Wald test and the likelihood ratio test was used to generate the F statistic p-value. Gene annotations were assigned using the custom annotation tables generated in-house as detailed in GL-DPPD-7110-A (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/blob/GL_RefAnnotTable-A_1.1.0/GeneLab_Reference_Annotations/Pipeline_GL-DPPD-7110_Versions/GL-DPPD-7110-A/GL-DPPD-7110-A.md), with STRINGdb (version 2.16.4), PANTHER.db (version 1.0.12), and org.Mm.eg.db (version 3.19.1). Assessment of ERCC spiked genes was performed as detailed in the ERCC_analysis_GLbulkRNAseq.html report.
